summary: Zambia's 2022 visa-waiver order scrapped visas for more than 50 countries — including the US, UK and the EU — so most tourists now enter visa-free for up to 90 days a year, while remaining nationalities apply online; the KAZA UniVisa adds seamless travel with Zimbabwe around Victoria Falls.

fee.notes: Covers both Zambia and Zimbabwe for 30 days, including unlimited crossings between them and day trips to Botswana via Kazungula. Issued on arrival at Lusaka and Livingstone airports and the Victoria Falls land borders to eligible nationalities.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on arrival in Zambia and should have at least two blank pages for stamps.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required only if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. Neighbouring countries may in turn ask for a certificate when you arrive from Zambia — check onward requirements.

travelInsurance.text: Not an entry requirement, but recommended — good private care exists in Lusaka, while safari areas rely on air evacuation.

onwardTicket.text: Not systematically checked, but airlines and immigration officers may ask for onward travel plans and accommodation details.

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published; visitors may be asked to show sufficient means for their stay.

currencyLimits.text: Travellers carrying more than about USD 5,000 (or the equivalent) in cash should declare it on arrival and departure — confirm the current threshold with the Zambia Revenue Authority.

notes: Drones require prior authorisation from the Zambia Civil Aviation Authority — bring the permit or expect the drone to be held at customs.

payments.text: Cards work in Lusaka and Livingstone hotels, supermarkets and fuel stations; markets and rural areas are cash-only. US dollars are widely accepted for safaris and visas, but bring newer-series notes in good condition.

safety.text: Zambia is one of the region's more stable, friendly destinations. Petty theft occurs in Lusaka and busy bus stations; on safari and around Victoria Falls the main risks are wildlife and roads rather than crime.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Zambia Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: May to October is the dry season — prime safari time, hot from September. Victoria Falls thunders fullest from about February to May; by late October the Zambian side can run nearly dry, when the Zimbabwean side keeps more water.

tips.text: Visiting both sides of Victoria Falls? The KAZA UniVisa (USD 50 on arrival at Livingstone or the falls borders) covers Zambia and Zimbabwe for 30 days with unlimited crossings, plus day trips to Botswana via Kazungula — usually cheaper than separate visas.

Victoria Falls is seasonal: spectacular spray February–May, while by October–November the Zambian side can be a trickle — that's when Devil's Pool trips run, and the Zimbabwean side offers better views.
Malaria is present in most of the country year-round, including Livingstone and the safari valleys — take prophylaxis, use repellent and sleep under nets.
Avoid intercity driving after dark — unlit trucks, pedestrians and animals on the road cause most serious accidents. Distances are long, so plan fuel stops and start early.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Zambia?
faq.answer: Most tourists don't. Zambia's 2022 waiver scrapped visas for more than 50 countries — including the US, UK, EU members, Canada, Australia and Japan — on top of SADC and Commonwealth exemptions, allowing up to 90 days per calendar year for tourism. Remaining nationalities apply online through the official Zambia Immigration e-services portal.

faq.question: What is the KAZA UniVisa?
faq.answer: A joint Zambia–Zimbabwe visa costing USD 50, valid 30 days, sold on arrival at Lusaka and Livingstone airports and the Victoria Falls borders to a wide list of nationalities. It allows unlimited crossings between the two countries and day trips into Botswana through Kazungula — ideal for seeing both sides of the falls.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Zambia?
faq.answer: Visa-free tourists may spend up to 90 days in Zambia per calendar year; officers typically stamp 30 days at entry, extendable at immigration offices. eVisa holders get 30 days, also extendable for genuine tourism.

faq.question: How do I get a Zambia eVisa and what does it cost?
faq.answer: Apply at eservices.zambiaimmigration.gov.zm with a passport scan and photo. Single-entry visas cost about USD 25 and are normally approved within 3–5 working days — apply at least a week before travel and carry a printed copy.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Zambia?
faq.answer: Only if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. Note the reverse trip matters too: some neighbours and onward destinations may ask for a certificate from travellers who passed through parts of Zambia — check your whole route.
